claims.statement: lib/security/token-routes.ts is the canonical registry of seven token-bearing route prefixes (/portal/verify, /cancel, /reschedule, /manage, /intake, /calendar-feed, /invitation), exporting `:token*` catch-all header patterns and a fixed [Redacted] placeholder that is deliberately not a hash, fingerprint or truncation of the credential.

canonicalizeTokenPaths replaces the credential based on the route prefix rather than the credential's shape, consumes trailing segments, query string and fragment, leaves unrelated ids intact, and never parses or percent-decodes the URL.

next.config.ts applies a global security-header block to every route and then, declared after it so its keys win, a token-route block on each registry pattern that sets X-Robots-Tag noindex,nofollow and Referrer-Policy no-referrer.

The global header baseline sets one-year HSTS with includeSubDomains and no preload, X-Frame-Options DENY, nosniff, Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin, an all-empty Permissions-Policy, and an enforced CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', 'unsafe-inline' kept, 'unsafe-eval' only in development, and connect-src limited to self, the Supabase host, Stripe and Vercel.
When NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL is missing or malformed at build time, the CSP connect-src falls back to wildcard https and wss *.supabase.co sources rather than failing the build.

The Sentry scrubber canonicalizes token paths first and then redacts emails, JWTs, bearer tokens, Supabase token shapes and phone-number runs from every string, and drops values under a deny-by-default list of auth, identifier and clinical keys.

Before a Sentry event leaves the process, request cookies, headers and query string are deleted, the request URL is token-canonicalized and stripped of query and fragment, console breadcrumbs are dropped entirely, and the user object loses email, username and IP address.

The server Sentry configuration sets sendDefaultPii false and installs the scrubber as beforeSend, beforeSendTransaction and beforeBreadcrumb, and a parity test requires all three runtimes to keep those hooks and every registry family to be canonicalized.
Production performance traces are sampled at 10% and development at 100%, while error events are not subject to that sampling rate.

The PostHog browser before_send hook fails closed: an event survives only if its $current_url is an exact canonical marketing route and its name is on the marketing allowlist, so app, booking, portal, token, login, payment, unknown-route and unparsable-URL events are dropped rather than redacted.

PostHog is initialized with session recording disabled, exception capture off, autocapture armed only on marketing URLs, the /ingest same-origin proxy as API host, and guardBrowserEvent as before_send.

A route-privacy test enumerates every dynamic route under app/ and fails unless each is registered as a token route or explicitly classified non-bearer with a written reason, so a new bearer route fails by default.

Calendar-feed tokens are 32 random bytes encoded base64url and are stored only as a SHA-256 hex digest; migration 0116 dropped the raw calendar_feed_token column and its index, which a DB test verifies on the migrated schema.

The calendar feed resolves the practitioner by token hash with the service-role client, returns a generic 404 for a short or unknown token, an inactive practitioner or any lookup error, excludes cancelled appointments, emits generic event titles and descriptions without client or service data, and is served private, no-store.
Waitlist invitation tokens are 32 random bytes hex-encoded in SQL with only their SHA-256 stored, so the raw token is returned once and a resend must mint a new link.

The invitation recipient-proof capability is kept in an httpOnly cookie whose HMAC binds it to the hash of the invitation token and to the database-issued expiry; without APPOINTMENT_SIGNING_SECRET nothing is treated as proven.

Appointment HMAC tokens and intake tokens each require a dedicated signing secret with no fallback to another key, and the secret getter throws when it is unset; intake verification is timing-safe and rejects expired payloads.

The public cancellation action collapses malformed, unknown and expired tokens to one generic error, and the manage action returns a single generic message for any non-success, so error shapes cannot reveal whether an appointment or token exists.

The public Upstash rate limiters fail open: with missing Upstash configuration or a backend error the request is allowed, missing configuration is logged once per instance (as an error in production), and identifiers are SHA-256 hashed before reaching Redis keys or logs.
Rate-limit client IP is taken from x-real-ip, then the first x-forwarded-for hop, and otherwise all callers share a single unknown_ip bucket.
Public slot fetches are limited to 60 per 60 seconds per (IP, slug), and public booking submits to 5 per 10 minutes per (IP, slug) and 3 per hour per (email, slug).
Token-route actions are rate-limited per hash(token):hash(IP) with per-class windows, and the limiter runs before token verification so a 429 reveals nothing about token validity.

The waitlist recipient-proof limiter fails open by an explicit decision, because failing closed would strand a prospect who has no other way to obtain the proof code their booking requires; its limits are imported from the delivery policy module rather than restated.

The browser analytics boundary declares its own six-prefix token list without /invitation/ instead of importing the canonical registry, and the parity test covers only next.config.ts and the Sentry scrubber.
The token-route registry header and docs/03_SECURITY_AND_PRIVACY.md both describe six token families without /invitation, while the registry and its parity test have seven.
docs/03_SECURITY_AND_PRIVACY.md and a calendar-feed token comment still describe the raw feed token as retained or read by the settings UI, although migration 0116 dropped the raw column.
The invitation route-privacy test header still says the invitation route does not exist and no prefix is added, although /invitation is registered and the route exists.
The intake signing-secret comment says apps without INTAKE_SIGNING_SECRET fail fast at startup, but the secret is read lazily, so the failure occurs when an intake token is first minted or verified.
The migration ledger records migration 0116, which dropped the raw calendar-feed token column after hash-only lookup was deployed, as applied.
